trial_court: 2nd Additional District Judge, Balodabazar, Civil Suit No. 20-A/2000
case_name: Sahodra Bai And Ors vs Rambai And Ors.

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Sahodra Bai, Damini Bai, Rohini, Sarita, Mohini (daughters of Gend Singh Chandrakar)
parties.respondent_defendant: Rambai, Rashmi, Vidhya, Santosh Kumar, Toran Kuamr, Rudranath (sons and daughters of Gend Singh Chandrakar), State of Chhattisgarh

facts_of_case: Partition dispute between family members; trial court declared share of wife and daughters in suit land measuring 8.152 hectares.

legal_principles.principle: In the absence of evidence contrary to the record, it appears that the property was self-acquired property of Gend Singh.
legal_principles.held: From the order of the Revenue court which is placed in the record of the trial Court, it appears that Gend Singh had two wives namely Ram Bai and Sahodra Bai.
keywords: recorded in the name of Gend Singh

legal_principles.principle: Daughters are entitled to share in the property of their father, as per Section 16(3) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
legal_principles.held: Ram Bai, Rashmi, Vidhya, Santosh and Toran will also get share in the property of Gend Singh.

outcome.final_order: Appellants' appeal against the judgment/decree dated 13-8-2001 was preferred under Section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

use_for_drafting: guidelines for filing a partition suit
practical tips for handling a joint family dispute
